Space & Defense Daily — Monday, Oct 26, 2026

And the Space Force moved a missile-warning satellite and a cislunar mission off ULA's Vulcan onto SpaceX's Falcon Heavy.

Space & Defense Daily, Monday Oct 26 (covers Friday through this morning)

Top stories: SpaceX restored full Starlink and Starshield service to Ukraine, though Musk still says Kyiv broke the terms of service. NASA laid out its plan for a crewed Moon landing in 2028. And the Space Force moved a missile-warning satellite and a cislunar mission off ULA's Vulcan onto SpaceX's Falcon Heavy.

NATO

  • Two NATO Assistant Secretaries General visited Kyiv to discuss Ukraine's winter needs and PURL, NATO's program that buys equipment like air defense for Ukraine. NATO: Officials visit Ukraine
  • Latvia found drone wreckage in the Alūksne district and believes the drone entered its airspace on Oct 18. Ukrainska Pravda: Latvia drone wreckage
  • For context from last week, Lithuania asked NATO to let pilots fire on drones they can only track by radar, after jets couldn't visually identify an armed drone. Stars and Stripes: Lithuania's drone rules push

European Union

  • EU antitrust officials are skeptical of the planned merger of the Airbus, Thales, and Leonardo space businesses, worried it would leave fewer suppliers for the IRIS² satellite network. A formal review may not start until early 2027, and OHB is threatening legal action. Politico Europe: Satellite merger
  • SAFE, the EU's €150B defense-loan program, has paid out about €13.5B to 11 countries. Hungary and Italy are taking less than their shares, which could free €10B to €20B for joint projects with Ukraine. Defence Deals: SAFE payouts
  • A Leonardo and Rheinmetall joint venture reportedly won $4.16B in Italian Army combat-vehicle and tank contracts, though neither company will confirm it. Defense News: Italian Army deals

United States

  • NASA briefed its faster Artemis plan, which includes a 2027 Orion crew flight in Earth orbit to test docking with lander hardware. NASA: Artemis acceleration plans
  • Under the new plan, Starship will dock with Orion in Earth orbit and carry it to the Moon, while Blue Origin will skip in-space refueling. NASA will fly whichever lander is ready first. NASA: Lander changes
  • Because of Vulcan's delays, the Space Force moved a missile-warning satellite, a cislunar surveillance payload, three GPS launches, and a Space Development Agency mission to SpaceX. SpaceNews: Launch reshuffle
  • The Space Force wants its first system for the region between Earth and the Moon fielded by late 2029. SpaceNews: Pentagon's cislunar plans
  • Six firms, including Anduril, Slingshot, and LeoLabs, won the first operational contracts under the Space Force's commercial space reserve, worth $1.37M in total. Breaking Defense: CASR contracts
  • Lt. Gen. Gagnon wants extra satellite-jamming equipment so units can absorb losses in a war. SpaceNews: Jamming arsenal
  • The Pentagon and Lockheed agreed on a 10-year F-35 framework that still needs approval from Congress. BAE also got a deal for up to 25,000 APKWS rocket guidance kits a year. Air & Space Forces: Daily Report
  • SpaceX launched 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg as it slows Falcon 9 flights and shifts toward Starship. Space.com: Starlink launch
  • I found no new NDAA or Golden Dome developments this weekend that I could confirm.

European space

  • The ESA Council advanced a European exploration plan ahead of the Dec 15 ministerial meeting in Rome, and member states raised concerns about the EU Space Act and the EU budget. ESA: Council outcomes
  • ESA's Hera probe made its second braking burn as it approaches the Didymos asteroids. ESA: Hera braking
  • Lunar Link, the radio hardware ESA built for NASA's paused Gateway station, is flight-ready, and ESA is studying how to reuse it as a lunar relay. ESA: Lunar Link

Global space and defense

  • Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield work again on drones moving faster than 400 km/h, and Trump confirmed he spoke with Musk about the restrictions. CNBC: Starlink restored
  • Russia launched 126 drones at Ukraine overnight Friday, and Ukraine says it downed or jammed 101 of them. Ukrinform: Overnight drone attack
  • China launched the Yaogan-50 spy satellite and six more Yaogan satellites on Friday. SpaceNews: China's Yaogan launches
